{{nihongo|'''Igatomega Shrine'''|伊賀留我神社}} is a Shinto shrine located in the {{ill|Hazu|ja|羽津地区|qid=Q109363581|lt=Hazu}} of {{ill|Yokkaichi|ar|يوكايتشي (ميه)|azb|یوکایچی، میه|ban|Yokkaichi, Mié|be|Іакаіты|bg|Йокаичи|ce|Йоккаити|ceb|Yokkaichi (lungsod sa Hapon)|ckb|یۆکایچی|cs|Jokkaiči (Mie)|de|Yokkaichi|eo|Jokkaiĉi|es|Yokkaichi|et|Yokkaichi|eu|Yokkaichi (Mie)|fa|یوکایچی، میه|fi|Yokkaichi|fr|Yokkaichi|ga|Yokkaichi|gl|Yokkaichi|hak|Yokkaichi-sṳ|hy|Յոկաիտի|id|Yokkaichi, Mie|it|Yokkaichi|ja|四日市市|ko|욧카이치시|lt|Jokaičis|mg|Yokkaichi|mzn|یوکای‌ایچی، میه|nl|Yokkaichi|nn|Yokkaichi|no|Yokkaichi|pl|Yokkaichi|pt|Yokkaichi|ro|Yokkaichi|ru|Йоккаити|sh|Jokkaichi|simple|Yokkaichi|sr|Јокаичи|sv|Yokkaichi|tg|Ёккаичи|th|ยกกาอิจิ|tl|Yokkaichi|tr|Yokkaichi|tt|Йоккаити|uk|Йоккаїті|ur|یوکیچی، مئی|vi|Yokkaichi, Mie|war|Yokkaichi, Mie|zh|四日市市|zh_classical|四日市市|zh_min_nan|Yokkaiti-chhī|zh_yue|四日市|qid=Q26410}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|Q128196|qid=Q128196}}. It is an {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishikinaisha}} (a shrine listed in the Engishiki), and its former shrine rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is also called Minami-Ikaruga Shrine<ref name="Yokkaichi City History">{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=History of Yokkaichi City |date=1961-3-31 |publisher=Yokkaichi City Hall |page=1616}}</ref>. In Shigefuku, Yokkaichi City, there is Kita {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ikaruga Shrine}}<ref name="Yokkaichi City History"/> (its enshrined deities are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu Ōhirume no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ōyamatsumi|abstract|Q386563|az|Ooyamatsimu|de|Ōyamatsumi|fa|اویاماتسومی|fr|Ōyamatsumi|hr|O-Yama-Tsu-mi|ja|オオヤマツミ|ko|오야마쓰미노카미|mni|ꯑꯣꯌꯃꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|ru|Ооямацуми|simple|Ōyamatsumi|sv|Ōyamatsumi|tr|Ōyamatsumi|zh|大山津見|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi no Kami}}, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sukunahikona no Mikoto}}). {{nihongo|'''Igatomega Shrine'''|伊賀留我神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]].

== History ==
The year of foundation is unknown. It is said that in the 18th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, when {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}} was traveling in search of a site for the grand shrine of {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602}}, she stopped in this area, and the deity was enshrined at that place<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mie Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines|url=http://kyoka.mie-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/%e4%bc%8a%e8%b3%80%e7%95%99%e6%88%91%e7%a5%9e%e7%a4%be/|access-date=2025-11-24}}</ref>. During the {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} era, the village was divided into north and south, becoming Shigefuku Village of the {{ill|Kuwana Domain|ast|Dominiu de Kuwana|es|Dominio de Kuwana|fa|قلمرو کووانا|fr|Domaine de Kuwana|ja|桑名藩|ko|구와나번|pt|Domínio de Kuwana|ru|Кувана (княжество)|qid=Q2887780}} and Hazu Village, an enclave of the {{ill|Oshi Domain|fr|Domaine d'Oshi|ja|忍藩|ru|Оси (княжество)|qid=Q3034405}}, and as a result, Ikaruga Shrine also came to exist side by side as northern and southern shrines<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mie Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines: Ikaruga Shrine (Shigefuku Kō)|url=http://kyoka.mie-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/%e4%bc%8a%e8%b3%80%e7%95%99%e6%88%91%e7%a5%9e%e7%a4%be-2/|access-date=2025-12-13}}</ref>.

== Enshrined deities ==
* Main deity: Amaterasu Ōmikami Aramitama
* (Enshrined together) {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōtoshi no Kami}}・Ōyamatsumi no Kami・{{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}}・one unidentified deity

== Annual festival ==
October 16
